title: Binary Tree Paths
prompt:
Given the `root` of a binary tree, return all root-to-leaf paths, formatted as strings where each path is written as node values joined by `"->"`, in any order.

The tree is given as a level-order array where `null` marks a missing child (the standard LeetCode serialization). Your function receives this array directly; the starter code includes a helper that builds the tree from it, so you only need to build and format the paths. For deterministic checking, return the paths in the order the left-then-right DFS discovers them.

examples.explanation: There are two root-to-leaf paths: 1->2->5 and 1->3.
With only a left child, node 2 is the single leaf, so there is exactly one root-to-leaf path.

constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [1, 100]
hints: Do a DFS from the root, keeping track of the path taken so far as you go.
Add the current node's value to the path before recursing into children; when you reach a leaf (no children), the accumulated path is complete and should be recorded.
Remember to explore the left child before the right child so the output order is deterministic, and format each completed path by joining its values with '->'.

solution.approach: Run a DFS from the root, maintaining a list of the values visited so far on the current path. At each node, append its value to the path; if it's a leaf, join the accumulated values with '->' and record the result. Otherwise recurse into the left child (if present) then the right child (if present), so paths are discovered in a consistent left-to-right order.
solution.timeComplexity: O(n^2) worst case due to path string building, O(n log n) typical
solution.spaceComplexity: O(h), h = tree height, excluding output
